deliverablePathPatches.note: Maintainer-approved amendments to an epic's declared deliverable path where the byte-locked registry.epics[].files[]/stages[].files path (extracted verbatim from the pinned planning sources, itself frozen to the baseline SHA current when the source was authored) collides with an unrelated existing artifact discovered during implementation, or is otherwise provably unbuildable as declared (BLOCKED-012's class: a forced same-stage deviation, e.g. a real dependency cycle). P6-07-C-lifecycle-discovery.reason: The pinned first100-requirements-matrix.md source (line 1134) names this exact path -- .e2e.ts is not a Writer naming choice, it is the sources own declared kind:N deliverable. Mechanical problem: first100-exact-sha.ymls Full test suite step (the workflow this program requires for ledger-greening observations) runs a bare `pnpm exec vitest run --reporter=json`, which uses vitest.config.tss default testIncludes (packages/*/*/tests/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx} only) -- it never discovers any *.e2e.ts file. Every other real .e2e.ts test in this repo (packages/e2b/e2b, packages/llm/llm-pi-ai, packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/packages/shell/bash-sandbox) is instead verified by its own dedicated CI workflow (e2b-e2e.yml / pi-ai-provider-e2e.yml / sandbox.yml), never by first100-exact-sha.yml -- widening the default includes glob to also discover .e2e.ts would pull those genuinely-external-resource-dependent suites into the main CI gate, a disproportionate blast radius for this one epics path. Renaming the actual deliverable to lifecycle.spec.ts is the only fix whose blast radius matches the problem: same test content, same assertions, discoverable by the same CI step every other epic already relies on. Verified byte-for-byte before approval: all 27 originally-frozen case titles are unchanged under the new path (0 missing); a 28th case (a createdAt-collision pagination-tiebreak test closing a GREEN-review-found coverage gap) was added separately during the GREEN corrective round, unrelated to this path patch.

P6-07-P-lifecycle-store.reason: Architecturally unrealizable as declared, not a convenience relocation -- a strictly stronger basis than a path-spelling correction. P6-07's declared P-stage deliverables sit in packages/session/session-persistence/src/, but a durable session-lifecycle registry must name SessionLifecycleRecord/SessionDisposition and call the C-stage's listSessions/assertNoLegalHold/hardErase/propagateDeletion. That import closes a real project-reference cycle, verified by running the compiler rather than by reading manifests: session-persistence -> session-lifecycle -> workspace/workspace -> session-persistence, where the latter two edges already exist (session-lifecycle peer-depends on dsh-workspace; workspace/workspace peer-depends on dsh-session-persistence). `pnpm exec tsc -b packages/session/session-persistence/tsconfig.json` reports TS6202 on a branch carrying the declared edge. No level of effort inside the declared scope avoids this: every P6-07 clause is an assertion about lifecycle semantics (must[0]'s filters ARE listSessions; acceptance[1]'s hold IS assertNoLegalHold; acceptance[2]'s propagation IS propagateDeletion), so a record-type-generic store that cannot name a disposition observes none of them and proves only that a JSON document round-trips. A variant exploiting tsconfig.host.json's direct inclusion of packages/*/*/tests/** (letting a test import what src/ may not) was also rejected: it would produce real observations while no shipped code assembles the service, making a fixture read as a product surface -- worse than an honest gap, because it greens. The reverse direction is acyclic and is the natural one: the package owning the decisions gains the durable store beneath them. session-lifecycle is not referenced by any other package's tsconfig (apps/web/tsconfig.json does reference it, but an application is a terminal consumer and does not enter the inter-package dependency graph), and session-persistence's transitive closure (cosmokit, cordis, brand, core/session) never reaches session-lifecycle, so this placement adds zero new dependency edges. Cross-package repointing is within this mechanism's established range -- see P0-06-U-session-replay, which repoints from core/session/src/types.ts into a different package. The epic's must/acceptance clauses are unchanged. Only the index.ts deliverable is repointed; coordinator.ts and revision.ts stay declared-but-unmodified, which is already the settled reading of a stage file list (it is a scope ceiling, not a quota) and is what this stage would have done in either placement -- PersistenceCoordinator's storage contract is keyed on SessionId and SessionEvent under SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION, and a lifecycle disposition is not a session-log event.

Build-infrastructure edits (plugin-compat/package.json gaining a ./solver export, app-boot's package.json/tsconfig.json dependency edge, pnpm-lock.yaml) are not patched: the P1-01.U precedent settles that a stage list is the deliverable scope, not an exhaustive change list (that commit touched 36 files against 5 declared). P6-07-U-query-projection-types.reason: Scope widening, not substitution: filters.ts and session-lifecycle/src/index.ts keep their declared work; cursor.ts stays read-not-modified for the second time, as the Contract stage already decided and documented (cursor encoding is provider-owned -- session-query-sqlite hand-rolls its own base64url JSON), and a stage list is a scope ceiling rather than a quota (precedent: P6-07.P's coordinator.ts/revision.ts). must[0] requires tenant/workspace/status filters over the real corpus, which the declared scope cannot reach. P6-07-U-sqlite-filter-refusal.reason: Compiler-forced consequence of the approved projection widening, not an independent deliverable. Adding 'tenant'/'workspace' to the SessionResultFilter union turns session-query-sqlite/src/query.ts's exhaustive switch into TS2345 ("not assignable to type 'never'"), so the repository does not typecheck until that switch handles the new clauses. Three options existed and only one is safe: the sqlite index has no tenant or workspace column, so silently dropping a tenant clause in ranked search would return ANOTHER TENANT'S sessions to a caller that explicitly asked to be scoped to its own -- a data-isolation defect, not a limitation. The clause is therefore refused with SESSION_QUERY_INVALID_FILTER, which is this repository's "misconfiguration fails loud" rule applied to a query the index genuinely cannot answer. Approved by the Supervisor without escalation because the alternatives are a security defect or a non-compiling tree; recorded here so the deviation is auditable rather than buried in a diff. Two accompanying cases in tests/tenant-filter-refusal.spec.ts sit outside the frozen command and are required by the per-file 100% coverage gate. The epic's must/acceptance clauses are unchanged.
